PullRequest.Title: chat: always enable turn status pills
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- remove the `chat.turnStatusPills` configuration and its legacy object compatibility path
- keep turn status pills enabled for Agent Host chat inputs, completed responses, and the Agents Window toolbar
- update tests and component fixtures to model Agent Host sessions directly instead of opting into the setting

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted ESLint on all changed TypeScript files
- `scripts\test.bat src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentHost\agentHostSessionInputPills.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatContentParts\chatTurnPillsPart.test.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts --timeout 15000`
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatListRenderer.test.ts --grep "turn status pills" --timeout 15000`

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch an Agent Host chat in the workbench chat view/editor and show live input status pills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget resolves the Agent Host session, acquires session state, resolves the active changeset, and acquires its state before change counts and metadata-backed pills can appear. Local browser-view enumeration and pill DOM updates are synchronous on this UI path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent Host protocol state subscription for the session snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical session resource per active widget; duplicate holders are ref-counted and share one wire subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The subscription already ran with the prior default-true setting; an explicit chat.turnStatusPills=false prevented it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The snapshot is required before metadata and changeset selection can resolve, although the rest of the chat remains usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent Host protocol state subscription for the selected changeset
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one selected changeset per active widget, shared by resource if another consumer already holds it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The subscription already ran by default; only explicit opt-outs suppressed it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The snapshot supplies the live changes count shown above the input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active Agent Host session/changeset per chat widget, plus scans over known browser views and session metadata collections when those observables change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session and changeset subscriptions start asynchronously; the subscription manager coalesces duplicate resource subscriptions by refcount. No unbounded parallel loop is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Active Agent Host subscriptions are shared while references remain; disposing the widget releases them and the last release unsubscribes. Browser data is local and recomputed on browser-view changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed gate and the subscription call path are explicit, and subscription-manager sharing/lifecycle are implemented in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote snapshot latency and the number of simultaneously instantiated chat widgets vary, but cardinality is bounded and the pre-PR default already enabled this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the PR intentionally makes an already-default-on, bounded live-status path unconditional. It adds cost only for users who explicitly opted out, without introducing new per-item fan-out or a lifecycle leak.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and scroll through completed responses in an Agent Host chat history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each completed response currently rendered by the virtualized list, the renderer creates a turn-pills content part. That part observes per-request diffs before deciding whether to display and eagerly constructs the collapsed file-list widget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host session/chat state and the request's turn changeset to resolve authoritative file changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Session and chat resources are shared across rendered rows; one distinct turn-changeset subscription exists per rendered completed turn that supports turn changesets. Virtualization limits concurrency to rendered/template-retained rows rather than total history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This same fan-out occurred under the old default true. An explicit false setting omitted all turn-pills parts and subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subscriptions determine whether the summary is visible; rendering the response itself proceeds while snapshots resolve.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of concurrently rendered completed response rows, and changed files in those rows. Diff aggregation scans all files; nested list rendering shows at most six rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Distinct turn subscriptions may start concurrently for visible rows; session/chat subscriptions are coalesced by resource. Rendered parts are disposed when templates are cleared/reused, releasing references.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-request observables are memoized in a 1000-entry LRU; active resource subscriptions are ref-counted. Warm rows reuse observables and shared snapshots, while cold turns require a changeset snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer gating, provider construction, lazy observable subscription, ref-counting, and virtualized row disposal were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport size, row heights, remote latency, and explicit opt-out prevalence vary. The mechanism is real but was already the default behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: always rendering these summaries is the stated product change, the prior default already did so, and active boundary cardinality is viewport-bounded and coalesced. There is no diff-introduced leak or unbounded history fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an Agents Window session whose workspace metadata references GitHub issues
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The session toolbar resolves issue references; when the Issues pill is visible it refreshes each issue model immediately so state/icons and rich hover details can update, then keeps open issues on a 15-minute poll schedule.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch/revalidate each referenced GitHub issue and periodically poll open issues
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model per distinct referenced issue. Concurrent callers for the same issue share a model and in-flight refresh; repeated on-demand refreshes are suppressed for 60 seconds and disposed snapshots are cached for 100 issues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The network path already ran when the setting's default true was in effect. Explicit chat.turnStatusPills=false prevented refresh/polling; per-kind Issues visibility still suppresses it after this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The pill can render from reference metadata before requests complete; live state and hover details update asynchronously, so network work is not blocking the overall view.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct GitHub issues referenced by the active session after model-key deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The autorun invokes refresh for each issue without a batch limiter, but per-key models coalesce duplicate/in-flight requests. Polling is one scheduler per distinct open issue at 15-minute intervals.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold issues perform a fetch; warm models share the current payload and refresh promise. Recently disposed models restore ETag/payload snapshots from a 100-entry LRU, allowing conditional revalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed gate directly controls the autorun, and fetch debounce, ETag caching, polling cadence, and model sharing are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions normally reference few issues, and only users who had disabled the old default-on setting see newly added requests. Exact API latency and issue counts vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: network work is asynchronous, per-kind visibility still gates it, and the diff makes the documented default behavior unconditional rather than introducing a new boundary or scaling pattern.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize configuration and session-pill visibility state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration registration no longer installs the chat.turnStatusPills schema, and pill controllers use constant enabled observables plus the existing per-kind visibility memento.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant configuration entries and eight pill kinds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous or concurrent boundary work is introduced on configuration initialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-kind hidden state remains persisted in application-scoped storage; removing the old schema removes its observable configuration listener.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff only deletes schema/observable configuration plumbing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; this is constant startup work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; this slightly reduces configuration registration and listener work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 12 changed files and traced the always-on input-pill, completed-turn rendering, Agents Window issue polling, configuration, subscription ownership, caching, virtualization, and disposal paths. The PR removes an explicit opt-out, but the prior default already exercised these bounded/coalesced paths; no high-confidence unintended performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
